title: Answers to Questions about the Book "How the Khilafah Was Destroyed"
text:
Answers to Questions

About the book "How the Khilafah Was Destroyed"

1 - The Ottoman State's entry into the war had as its basic purpose, as was announced, the recovery of the lands the State had lost, and in particular the recovery of Egypt from the English, who had entered it temporarily on account of the debt but then took control of it. That is why the first battles on the Ottoman front were in Egypt. They thought that by entering the war on the side of Germany they would recover some of the regions.

In that period intellectual and political weakness had become rampant in the Ottoman State, so they did not grasp the dimensions of this war, neither from the standpoint of the Shari'ah rule nor from the standpoint of political awareness of its dimensions. Added to this was the penetration of the Kuffar, especially the English, through agents among the Arabs and the Turks, and so the war ended in the well-known tragic ending.

2 - Russia's share from signing the Sykes-Picot agreement was nothing but moral. Its share was no more than building a good relationship with England and France, hoping that the two states would turn a blind eye to it in some of what it coveted of the lands of the Ottoman State, especially the region of (Erzurum) in the east of Turkey, in addition to having the privilege of protecting the Orthodox Christians in Palestine. That is why the texts of the agreement stated, in Article Three:

(An international administration shall be established in the area called (Palestine), the form of which is to be decided upon after consultation with Russia ...). And after this agreement, which was concluded in 1916, Russia afterwards, in 1917, occupied (Erzurum).

3 - As for Mustafa Kemal, much has been written about his lineage and origin, and the most likely view is that his origin is doubtful, whether he was from the Dönmeh Jews or from other spiteful Kuffar. Professor (Muwaffaq Bani Marjeh), in his book (The Awakening of the Sick Man), quoted Dr. Riza Nur, who held the post of deputy foreign minister in the era of Mustafa Kemal, and who then wrote his memoirs, which he deposited with France and Britain on the condition that they not be published before 1960. They were published in Turkey in '68 and caused a great uproar because of the (Kemalist) scandals they contained, and they were confiscated by the Turkish state. He quoted the following from him in those memoirs:

(Mustafa Kemal was the illegitimate child of a woman from Salonika called Zubaida, who was known for her bad conduct, and she attributed her son to one of the customs guards in Salonika named Ali Riza Efendi, whom she later married). Even so, Mustafa Kemal carried out criminal acts against the Khilafah and Islam the like of which the Jews, the English and the rest of the Kafir colonialists did not do.

Accept my greetings.

On 01/07/2004 CE.
